results.why: The plant is that tightly scoped destination service accounts break Server-Side Diff because diff needs patch authority everywhere, whereas the claim asserts the opposite route — that diff ignores destinationServiceAccounts entirely and so leaves an audit-attribution gap.

The plant is that impersonation and the user/group RBAC request are the same governance shift, so reviews and audit must follow the service-account identity, while the claim asserts the two proposals move identity in opposite directions and split access review across two RBAC systems.

The claim states the same chain: commitAuthor copied forward from the dry commit onto a push made by a shared machine credential, with signing opt-in and defaulting to false, leaving an unverifiable authorship record.

The claim states the same chain: rollback pushes bypass the commit server where signing lives, so signature-requiring branches reject them and the operator sees only a failed push with no signing explanation or recovery path.
